projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

version-declared.name: Python version is declared
version-declared.description: The project declares the Python version it is built and run against, and that version is no older than the configured floor.
version-declared.remediation: Declare the interpreter where the project already describes itself: `requires-python = ">=3.12"` under `[project]` in `pyproject.toml`, or a `.python-version` file naming the exact release. Without one, the interpreter is whatever the runner happens to have, so a syntax or standard library difference shows up in CI instead of on the laptop where it was introduced.

minVersion.description: Oldest Python version accepted. A declared version below this is a violation.

lockfile-committed.name: Python dependencies are locked
lockfile-committed.description: The project commits a lock file, so an install of the same commit resolves the same versions.
lockfile-committed.remediation:
Commit the lock file your installer writes:

```bash
uv lock          # writes uv.lock
poetry lock      # writes poetry.lock
pip-compile      # writes requirements.txt from requirements.in
```

A `>=` or `~=` requirement resolves to whatever the index serves that day, so without a lock file the build that shipped is not the build that was reviewed.

single-lockfile.name: One installer owns the environment
single-lockfile.description: The project commits at most one lock file, so two installers don't both try to manage the environment.
single-lockfile.remediation: Pick the installer the project actually uses and delete the other lock files. A checkout with both `poetry.lock` and `uv.lock` installs different versions depending on which command the developer or CI step runs. The lock file nobody uses drifts silently until someone does use it.

build-backend-declared.name: Build backend is declared
build-backend-declared.description: A packaged project names its build backend in `[build-system]`, so it builds the same way everywhere.
build-backend-declared.remediation:
Declare the backend in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

Without a `[build-system]` table, PEP 517 falls back to legacy setuptools at whatever version the environment has, so the wheel a release produces depends on the machine that built it.
